To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of Calsequestrin is an EF hand calcium binding protein with a four helix bundle.

Calsensin adopts an EF‐hand‐like structure, that the calcium‐binding site is formed by two EF‐hand motifs, and that calcium binding is associated with slow conformational changes in one of the helices.
Calsensin adopts a unicornate‐like four‐helix structure in the calcium bound state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the three‐dimensionall solution structure of a calcium‐binding protein, Calsensin.
the elucidation of the structure and function of proteins involved in the development and maintenance of the nervous system.
the molecular mechanism of calcium binding and release by the EF‐hand family of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Calsensin represents a novel type of EF‐hand calcium binding protein that has evolved to fulfill the specific functional requirements of its invertebrate neuronal host.
Calsensin has a structure and calcium‐binding characteristics similar to those of calmodulin.
Calsensin has a unique structure that is not found in any other calcium‐binding protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of Calsequestrin, a calcium‐binding protein that is a component of the sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle, is a single four‐helix domain.
we determined the solution structure of Calsen‐sin, a novel EF‐hand protein from invertebrate nervous system, and we characterized its backbone dynamics.

we have solved the structure of a new member of a family of EF‐hand calcium binding proteins and that the structure of this protein is very similar to other members of this family, but the dynamics are quite different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Calsensin represents a novel member of the EF‐Hand protein family that is expressed in the peripheral nervous system and is a potential target for drug design.
Calsensin has a unique structure and calcium‐binding mechanism.
Calsensin has an unusual EF‐hand calciumbinding motif that is likely to be involved in calcium sensing.
